posts.text:
A mouse in a zero-oxygen chamber dies in under a minute.

A naked mole rat lasts 18 minutes and walks away.
comments: It switches to anaerobic metabolism running on fructose instead of glucose, which sidesteps the exact step where normal glycolysis stalls without oxygen. Plants use this pathway. No other mammal is known to use it as a whole-body rescue.

posts.text:
Your cat cannot taste that cake.

A mutation disabled the feline sugar taste receptor long ago, so sweetness simply does not register.

So what is your cat actually begging for?
comments: Cats are one of the only mammals that physically cannot taste sweetness. Whatever the begging is about, it is not the sugar.

posts.text:
Pinch the tail of an adult Pacific hagfish and you get about 0.9 liters of slime.

That is roughly seven times the volume of the animal that made it.
comments: Almost none of it is hagfish. It releases a small amount of dense exudate, and the exudate captures seawater, expanding up to 10,000 times in about 400 milliseconds.

posts.text:
Mike the Headless Chicken survived because a chicken's brain is not where you would guess.

The brain stem sits low and toward the back, angled into the neck. The axe missed it.
comments: It took the beak, face, eyes and most of the skull. It also missed the jugular, and a clot formed fast enough to stop him bleeding out.

posts.text:
A chameleon's tongue briefly pulls more G-force than a human fighter pilot can withstand.

It strikes a full body-length away and snaps back with its prey in a fraction of a second.
comments: A full body-length out and back again, in a fraction of a second.

posts.text:
Giraffes were long thought to be nearly silent.

Then researchers recorded over 947 hours of zoo audio and found them humming, only at night.

Did you assume giraffes made no sound?
comments: The hum averages 92 Hz. That is not infrasound, it sits well inside human hearing. They were audible all along. Nobody had listened for 947 hours.

posts.text:
Male seahorses do not just carry eggs. They gestate them.

The pouch seals shut and the embryos become embedded in his tissue.
comments: The pouch wall handles gas exchange and feeding like a placenta. The difference is what it is built from: a mammal's placenta grows from embryonic tissue, a seahorse's is converted skin.

posts.text:
A dog's sense of smell is estimated at 10,000 to 100,000 times more sensitive than a human's.

That wet nose is part of how it works.
comments: The moisture traps scent chemicals so they can be analyzed more effectively.

posts.text:
Dung beetles steer by the Milky Way.

With it visible, they crossed a two meter arena in about 40 seconds. Under cloud, the same crossing took close to two minutes.
comments: A beetle that keeps turning covers far more ground for the same distance. That gap is also what light pollution costs an animal, measured directly.

posts.text:
Wood frogs survive freezing.

Southern ones handle about -3C to -6C. Alaskan wood frogs of the same species survive to at least -16C.

How cold does it get where you are?
comments: The gap comes mostly from urea banked during autumn. Subarctic frogs stockpile roughly eight times the plasma urea of temperate ones before any ice appears.

posts.text:
When threatened, some sea cucumbers expel their own internal organs through their rear end.

Then they regrow a full set within weeks.
comments: The ejected organs are there to confuse predators. A full replacement set grows back within weeks.

posts.text:
A clownfish fits in your palm.

The oldest females are estimated to live around 30 years, roughly twice any other coral reef damselfish.

Would you have guessed that long?
comments: That is why their breeding queue works: a fish waiting for a slot may genuinely be queuing for decades.
